faqs.question: What is the difference between an ATS and recruiting CRM?
faqs.answer: An applicant tracking system organizes requisitions and candidates through the hiring process. A recruiting CRM emphasizes sourcing, talent pools and ongoing candidate relationships. Products can overlap, so verify the exact workflows and modules offered.

faqs.question: How should a recruiting team compare platforms?
faqs.answer: Run the same test vacancy through requisition approval, application review, interview scheduling, feedback collection, candidate communication, reporting and handoff to HR. Record friction, permissions and missing features.

faqs.question: What privacy issues should buyers review?
faqs.answer: Review candidate consent, retention and deletion, access controls, audit trails, data export, vendor subprocessors and applicable local employment/privacy rules. Get legal advice for jurisdiction-specific obligations.

author: Emily Nakamura
body:
Recruiting Software: ATS and Hiring Workflow Tools to Evaluate

Recruiting software should support the team's actual hiring process, from opening a requisition to communicating with candidates and handing successful hires to HR. The best fit depends on whether you are an in-house talent team, a staffing agency, or a growing business with a small HR function. This guide is a workflow-based shortlist, not a verified ranking. Current prices, ratings and plan-specific features have not been independently verified by PilotStack.

Platforms to evaluate

Greenhouse: Evaluate it for structured hiring, interview coordination and hiring-team collaboration. Test how the product supports your approval stages, interview kits, feedback, reporting and required integrations. Confirm the exact package and implementation scope.

Lever: Evaluate it when applicant tracking and candidate relationship workflows need to work together. Confirm the current feature set, automation, data export and the difference between included and optional modules.

BambooHR: Evaluate it when recruiting needs to connect with a broader HR workflow. Verify whether the current offer includes the applicant-tracking capabilities you need, the relevant plan limits and integrations with your other systems.

Rippling: Evaluate it when recruiting must connect with broader employee administration. Confirm the specific recruiting module, supported countries, integrations and the full contract scope rather than assuming all capabilities are included.

What to test in a trial

  • Create and approve a requisition and assign hiring-team roles.
  • Receive applications, identify duplicates and move candidates through stages.
  • Schedule interviews across time zones and collect structured feedback.
  • Send candidate communications and manage consent or opt-out preferences.
  • Build a report for time-to-hire, stage conversion and source quality.
  • Export candidate records and check what happens to notes, attachments and audit history.
  • Test the handoff to HRIS, payroll or onboarding tools.

Privacy, fairness and administration

Candidate records are sensitive. Review role-based access, retention and deletion, audit logs, data export, vendor subprocessors and relevant local employment and privacy requirements. If the platform offers automation or candidate scoring, ask how it works, what data it uses, how decisions are reviewed, and how human oversight is maintained. Legal requirements vary by jurisdiction; get appropriate advice for your hiring locations.

Compare total cost

Ask vendors to quote the same number of recruiters and hiring managers, expected requisitions, job-board needs, integrations, implementation and support. Clarify billing units, modules, minimum contract length, renewal terms and exit/export options. Prices are not independently verified in this guide, so do not rely on historical figures from third-party comparison pages.

Choose based on workflow fit

Score the finalists against your must-have tasks, user experience, reporting, integrations, privacy controls, migration effort and total cost. Document any gap that would require a workaround. Choose the system that supports your hiring process reliably, rather than assuming one vendor is best for every organization.
